metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth are counted as uptime metrics for AI data centers, because a degraded fabric wastes GPU-hours before it causes an outage.

The metric sits in the same category as UPS battery health, generator runtime, and SLA uptime compliance. That placement is the point. Availability for an AI facility is not only a question of whether power reached the racks, it is also a question of whether the network between them performed well enough for the work to finish. A facility can hold its power up and still fail its tenants.

For AI specifically, the cost of degradation lands on compute. Distributed training spreads a single job across many accelerators that must exchange state continuously, so latency and loss translate directly into idle expensive hardware. The definition covers both the internal fabric and external transit, which means the measurement spans the boundary between the building and the networks it depends on.

What the data does not provide is any measurement. There are no latency figures, no loss thresholds, no bandwidth targets, no sampling interval, and no indication of how often these values breach acceptable ranges. It defines what would be watched and why, not what was found.
